title: How Many Of Each Title
description:
Report each job title and the number of employees holding it, but only for titles held by **two or more** people.

Name the columns `title` and `headcount`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY title
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hint: Filtering on an aggregate is HAVING, not WHERE.
outputExplanation: Three employees are Engineers, two are Managers, and two are Reps. Analyst is held by only one person and is not reported.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
No title has two or more employees
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','Eng',100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','Mgr',100,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'C','Rep',100,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Every title has two or more employees
NULL title appears twice — qualifies
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A',NULL,100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B',NULL,100,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Mix — some titles qualify, some do not
All employees share the same title
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','Eng',100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','Eng',100,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'C','Eng',100,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');
